note: RFC 1334 Section 2.2.2: "If the Peer-ID/Password pair received in a Authenticate-Request is not recognizable or acceptable, then the authenticator MUST transmit a PAP packet with the Code field set to 3 (Authenticate-Nak), and SHOULD take action to terminate the link." The earlier weak verdict rested on the clause 'a PAP packet': TestPAPRejectWritesNak discarded the Protocol. 83deb89129 makes it read the Protocol and assert proto == ProtoPAP on the reject reply, so a Code 3 framed under another Protocol now goes red by reading. Code 3 is asserted by the same unit, and TestPAPRequestEmitsEvent asserts Ack on accept, so an unconditional Nak goes red; the recorded mutant inverts the branch at pap.go:258. Caveat on proof: no record shows the new assertion red. The positive record panics WritePAPNak, which fails before any assertion is reached, and pap.go:250 frames both replies under one WriteFrame(ProtoPAP). The tagged units compare the symbolic constant; the literal Code 3 is pinned by the untagged TestPAPWriteNak (0x03). The SHOULD half is RFC1334-2.3-5 and is not claimed here.
